newsitem.title: UK: Netherlands copper stock anomaly could be CIS data.
newsitem.headline: Netherlands copper stock anomaly could be CIS data.

text.p: The discrepancy in copper stocks data in the Netherlands reported by the World Bureau of Metal Statistics (WBMS) may reflect problems regarding CIS figures, industry specialists Bloomsbury Minerals Economics (BME) said.
Last week the WBMS said nearly 600,000 tonnes of non-LME copper may have built up in Netherlands bonded warehouses between 1991 and 1995.
BME said in its latest statistical supplement that it was unlikely that 600,000 tonnes of stock could build up in total secrecy.
The start of the problem coincides with the beginning of large scale trans-shipments of copper from the CIS through Rotterdam.
"BME suspects that a proportion of the poorer grades of CIS wirebars and cathodes may be entering Rotterdam as refined copper and leaving listed as blister-equivalent," it said.
However, whether this explains the main part of the 120,000 tonne a year discrepancy is unclear. Transit trade data for blister and scrap might clarify the picture, BME added.
